A 56-year-old female patient with no significant medical history or current medications comes to her
primary care provider for her yearly check-up. She expresses anxiety about potentially developing
hepatitis C after learning about her friend's chronic HCV infection. Laboratory results show elevated
liver enzymes with AST of 55 U/L and ALT of 102 U/L. Her hepatitis antibody screening returns
negative. What should be the most appropriate next step in her management? Answer Choices: (A)
Perform FibroScan elastography (B) Administer sofosbuvir-velpatasvir (C) Perform liver biopsy (D)
Check autoimmune markers (ANA, ASMA) (E) Check serum HCV RNA (F) Assess alcohol
consumption history (G) Check serum GGT (H) Assess for HCV exposure within the past 6 months (I)
Order abdominal ultrasound (J) Check hepatitis B serology
 A. Check serum GGT
B. Order abdominal ultrasound
C. Perform FibroScan elastography
D. Perform liver biopsy
E. Check autoimmune markers (ANA, ASMA)
F. Assess for HCV exposure within the past 6 months
G. Administer sofosbuvir-velpatasvir
H. Assess alcohol consumption history

I. Check hepatitis B serology
J. Check serum HCV RNA
